summary: Tested customer email/password auth end to end: backend through pytest (22 tests) and the mobile web preview at 390x844 with Playwright. Registration validation, phone OTP before account creation, upgrading a phone-only account (same id kept), email verification, email login, forgot/reset, and resetting email_verified_at on PATCH all work. Two problems found. (1) CRITICAL frontend: on a fresh install, 'Continuer en tant qu'invité' (login-guest) and a successful email login both send the user back to /onboarding instead of home. (2) Backend security: the per-email brute-force lockout is keyed on the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For value and is stored in memory per worker, so rotating the header bypasses it completely.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout can be bypassed. The bucket is f'login-email:{email}' keyed by IP, and _client_ip() trusts the LEFT-MOST X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls. Sending a different X-Forwarded-For on each request gave 10 straight 401s with no 429. The 'per-email' lockout is also really per (email, IP), so a distributed attacker is never limited. Counters live in memory in each of the 4 uvicorn workers, so enforcement is inconsistent (with a fixed spoofed header, 8 attempts through requests.Session got no 429; with plain curl the 429 came on the 7th attempt).

minor.issue: The per-email limit (6 per 15 min) counts successful logins too, because check_rate_limit runs before the password check. A real user who logs in 7 times in 15 minutes gets locked out. Count only failures, or reset the counter on success.

Only a non-unique index exists on lower(email). Two registrations or a PATCH running at the same time can both pass the email_taken check and create duplicate emails. Add a unique partial index on lower(email) where deleted_at is null.

Timing side channel: verified accounts trigger an SMTP send inside the request, while unknown emails return at once. The difference reveals whether an account exists. Send the email in a background task.

ui_bugs.issue: completeOnboarding() is only called in otp.tsx and in welcome.tsx guest(). On a fresh install, login-guest does router.replace('/'), and the (tabs)/_layout sees onboardingDone=false and redirects to /onboarding. Successful email login, password reset and Google login go through finishAuthFlow, which has the same problem. Reproduced: Passer, Passer, Continuer avec mon numéro, then login-guest ends on /onboarding; email login with awa.kone ends on /onboarding. Fix: call completeOnboarding() in login-guest and in every auth success path (for example inside finishAuthFlow or from the session signIn).

issues: Opening /verify-email without an email param shows 'envoyé à .' (empty email). Fall back to the signed-in customer's email.
The dev code label is inconsistent: the OTP screen says 'Code de test (pré-production) : xxxxxx', while verify-email and forgot say 'DEV: xxxxxx'.
The new password has no confirm field, unlike registration. Optional.

action_items: CRITICAL: call completeOnboarding() in the login-guest handler and in every auth success path (email login, forgot reset, Google, verify-email). Today a fresh-install user who uses these is sent back to /onboarding.

HIGH: make the login brute-force limit trustworthy. Use the right-most or ingress-appended X-Forwarded-For hop (or a trusted-proxy count) instead of the left-most entry. Key the email lockout on the email alone, not (email, IP). Store counters in Redis or the DB (Redis is already running) instead of per-worker memory.
Count only failed attempts toward the email lockout.
Add a unique index on lower(email) for customers that are not deleted.
Optional: send the forgot-password email in a background task to remove the timing difference; fix the empty email on verify-email when it is opened without a param.
critical_code_review_comments: rate_limit._client_ip trusts the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry, so every check_rate_limit bucket in the app can be bypassed (register-start, pw-forgot, pw-reset, login-email).
register_verify checks challenge attempts only, not attempts on the registration row. Each /register/resend gives 5 fresh guesses; resend is limited to 6 per hour per spoofable IP.
_find_or_create_customer_by_google clears an unverified email from an existing account (existing.email=None). Correct for ownership, but that user silently loses email login. Consider notifying them.
Good: Argon2id, codes stored as hashes, the same 401 message for wrong password and unknown email, and a dummy hash to equalise timing on unknown emails.

success_rate.backend: 91% (20/22; both failures are the rate-limit issue)
success_rate.frontend: 85% (all flows work once onboarding_done is set by hand; the guest and email-login landing bug is open)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Mobile preview: the Stack keeps hidden screens in the DOM, so scope selectors to the visible screen (page.locator('[data-testid=register-screen]').last...). To skip onboarding: localStorage.setItem('baked_onboarding_done','true'), then go to /api/app-preview/login. Pytest gives each request a random X-Forwarded-For to avoid in-memory rate limits (that is the bypass reported above). login-whatsapp shows its info message only once a valid 8+ digit phone is entered; otherwise it shows the phone error, which is by design.
rca of the issue: Onboarding bug: (tabs)/_layout.tsx redirects to /onboarding while onboardingDone is false, and the flag is only set by completeOnboarding(), which is called only in otp.tsx and welcome.tsx guest(). The new auth entry points (login-guest, email-login, forgot reset, Google) skip it. Repro: fresh browser, Passer x2, Continuer avec mon numéro, then login-guest or email login, and you land on /onboarding. Rate-limit bypass: the key is xff.split(',')[0], the client-supplied value. Repro: POST /api/auth/login/email 10 times with a wrong password, each with a different X-Forwarded-For; all return 401 and none return 429.
